Let's be honest, that green and black stuff growing on your siding isn't a great look. After a typical Nebraska winter and a humid Omaha summer, it’s amazing how fast dirt, algae, and general grime can build up on your house, driveway, and deck. You might not even notice how dingy it's gotten until you see a clean spot. That's where we come in.

My name is Bryan, and at A1, we do more than just haul junk and trim trees. We’ve got the equipment and the know-how to safely and effectively pressure wash your home’s exterior, making it look cared for and clean again. It’s one of the fastest ways to boost your curb appeal without spending a fortune on a new paint job.

More Than Just a Pretty House

Sure, a clean house looks great, but pressure washing is about more than just appearances. That green stuff, which is usually algae or mildew, can hold moisture against your siding. Over time, this can lead to rot and decay, especially on wood siding. On your driveway and walkways, that same algae can become incredibly slippery and dangerous when it gets wet.

Getting rid of that buildup isn't just cleaning; it's preventative maintenance. It protects the investment you have in your home. We can blast away years of accumulated dirt, pollen, and pollution, revealing the true color of your siding and concrete. It’s a satisfying transformation that also helps protect your property value.

What Can We Wash? Pretty Much Everything

People are often surprised by how many surfaces can be safely cleaned with a pressure washer when it's in the right hands. It’s not just for driveways. We can completely rejuvenate the look of your property by cleaning various areas. If you're getting ready for a seasonal cleanup, adding a pressure wash can make a huge impact.

Vinyl & Wood Siding

We gently remove algae, mildew, and dirt without forcing water behind the panels.

Driveways & Sidewalks

Erase dirt, oil spots, and grime to make your concrete look bright and clean.

Decks & Patios

We safely clean wood and composite decking, as well as brick or stone patios.

Fences & Retaining Walls

Bring back the original color of your wood fence or stone retaining wall.

Don't DIY Your Siding Off

You can rent a pressure washer from the hardware store, sure. But using one without experience can cause a lot of expensive damage. It’s incredibly easy to use too much pressure and etch lines into your wood deck, chip your siding, or blast the seals out of your windows. We’ve seen it happen all over Omaha.

When you hire us, you're not just getting a machine. You're getting our experience. We know exactly what pressure levels, nozzles, and cleaning solutions to use for each specific material. We work safely and efficiently, protecting your plants and property while getting the job done right the first time. No guesswork, no damage, just a clean home.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you pressure wash a wood deck without damaging it?

Absolutely. We use a lower pressure setting and the right nozzle for soft woods like cedar or pine. It's about using the right technique to clean the grime off without stripping the wood or leaving marks.

How often should I have my house pressure washed in Nebraska?

For most homes in the Omaha area, every 2 to 3 years is a good rule of thumb. That green algae and mildew loves our humid summers, especially on the north side of the house, so washing it off prevents it from getting out of hand.

Will pressure washing get oil stains off my driveway?

It can definitely make a big difference. While some deep-set oil stains might leave a faint mark, our commercial-grade equipment and cleaners can lift the majority of fresh and surface-level stains from concrete, significantly improving the look.

Is there a difference between power washing and pressure washing?

Yes, the main difference is heat. Power washing uses heated water, which is great for breaking down tough, greasy stains. We use the term pressure washing, but we use heated water when it's needed for the job.
